description:
intent=i025 snapshot=s04 branch=header-accessor-no-linearize status=complete
finding location=net/ncsi/ncsi-rsp.c:35-87 confidence=high conclusion=NCSI response validation reads attacker-length-driven checksum bytes via skb_network_header() with no pskb_may_pull and no skb->len bound, giving a remotely injectable OOB read past the linear head (up to ~64KB).
finding location=net/ncsi/ncsi-rsp.c:1185-1233 confidence=medium conclusion=ncsi_rcv_rsp and the NCSI response handlers dereference skb_network_header() pointers (hdr->type/id/length and 204-byte struct copies) with no linearization guarantee, so a non-linear NCSI frame reads past the linear head.
finding location=net/ncsi/ncsi-aen.c:209-247 confidence=medium conclusion=ncsi_aen_handler dereferences skb_network_header()-derived AEN header fields and payload-relative checksum words with no linearization or skb->len check, so short/non-linear AEN frames read past the linear head.
unresolved location=net/ieee802154/6lowpan/rx.c:68 conclusion=Follow up: audit 802.15.4 RX skb allocation in drivers/net/ieee802154 and any virtual ieee802154 netdev to confirm the first payload byte is always in the linear head before the *skb_network_header(skb) dispatch reads at net/ieee802154/6lowpan/rx.c:68.
unresolved location=net/mac802154/llsec.c:631 conclusion=Follow up: verify every mac802154 RX skb is fully linear (mac_len + payload inside the head) before the sg_init_one(skb_mac_header(skb), assoclen + datalen) crypto scatterlists at net/mac802154/llsec.c:680 and 887.
coverage_gap=The ~230 net/ and drivers/net/ files with only one or two header-accessor uses (mostly TX checksum/GSO/tunnel output paths in ethernet drivers) were density-ranked but never opened or per-function audited.
coverage_gap=net/ipv6/exthdrs.c, net/ipv6/ndisc.c, net/ipv6/mcast.c, net/openvswitch/flow.c, net/netfilter/nf_flow_table_*.c and net/core/drop_monitor.c have many accessor dereferences but were only name-triaged from grep line counts, not read.
coverage_gap=No NCSI-capable driver other than ftgmac100 was surveyed for scatter-gather/GRO RX delivery of ETH_P_NCSI frames, so the non-linear precondition of the ncsi_rcv_rsp/ncsi_aen_handler dereferences stays unproven.
coverage_gap=No KASAN build, crafted 0x88F8/6lowpan frame, or runtime reproducer was run; head/headlen behavior is argued purely from source.
limitation=All findings are static source-reading hypotheses: the ncsi_validate_rsp_pkt over-read is provable from the unbounded payload arithmetic, but no kernel was built or packet injected to observe it.
limitation=The NCSI findings require a registered NCSI netdev with a pending enabled request (nr->enabled at ncsi-rsp.c:1218), so the attacker must inject on the NC-SI management channel during probing; reachability is narrower than the seed's phonet path.
limitation=The 12-candidate budget bounded the audit: hsr, xfrm, ipvs and act_nat were classified from pull-call co-location seen via grep plus partial reads rather than full enclosing-function reads of every accessor site.
limitation=The snapshot has no git history, so it cannot be determined whether upstream has since added pskb_may_pull or length checks to net/ncsi, net/ieee802154/6lowpan/rx.c or net/mac802154/llsec.c.
limitation=Accessors wrapped in macros or helper inlines outside the seven literal grep terms (e.g. ipv6_hdr()/tcp_hdr()/ip_hdr()) were outside this branch's literal search and could hide additional unguarded receive-path dereferences.
artifact=findings/i025.json
